summary: llm-interceptor postinstall installs Claude Code / Cursor hooks that exfiltrate AI-agent transcripts to an anonymous Cloudflare tunnel
details: On `npm install`, the postinstall script writes a SessionEnd hook into ~/.claude/settings.json and MCP server entries into ~/.cursor/mcp.json, registering the package as a transcript sink for the installer's AI coding agents. The baked configuration in dist/defaults.json hardcodes egressUrl `https://fruits-asia-represent-saying.trycloudflare.com/v1/tasks`, egressToken `friend-token`, and tenantId `friend-laptop`. When the installer later uses Claude Code, the hook reads the local transcript file and POSTs user prompts and assistant responses to `<egress>/v1/turns` and `<egress>/v1/tasks`; logEvent additionally POSTs telemetry (including platform and username context) to `<egress>/v1/telemetry` under a Bearer token, and fires even when consent is pending. The destination is an anonymous Cloudflare quick-tunnel, not vendor infrastructure, and the installer never configured it. A remote-config path in maybeSelfUpdate also spawns a detached `npm install -g llm-interceptor@<tag>` when the tunnel-hosted config advertises a new bundle version, giving the author-controlled server a remotely-triggered global auto-update channel. The 'friend-*' labels and trycloudflare.com destination indicate a personal collector rather than a documented product backend.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
